data.title: Exidavnemab Phase 2a study successfully concluded - preparing for Phase 2b
data.description:
Exidavnemab Phase 2a study successfully concluded - preparing for Phase 2b

Exidavnemab Phase 2a study successfully concluded - preparing for Phase 2b

PR Newswire

STOCKHOLM, Nov. 23, 2026

STOCKHOLM, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- BioArctic AB (publ) (NASDAQ STOCKHOLM: BIOA B) today announced topline results from the completed Phase 2a EXIST study evaluating exidavnemab in patients with Parkinson's disease (PD) and multiple system atrophy (MSA). In the study, exidavnemab was well tolerated and showed a favorable safety profile across all dose groups and patient populations studied.

Exidavnemab is a monoclonal antibody that selectively targets aggregated pathological forms of α-synuclein, while sparing the physiological forms i.e. the monomers. Aggregation of pathological α-synuclein is increasingly recognized as a defining characteristic of several progressive neurodegenerative diseases, including PD and MSA.

The randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2a EXIST study was designed primarily to evaluate the safety, tolerability and pharmacokinetics (how the body processes the drug) of repeated dosing of exidavnemab. In total, 38 participants were randomly assigned in a 2:1 ratio to receive exidavnemab or placebo. Following an interim safety review of 13 participants in the first cohort, where a lower dose was evaluated, 13 additional participants with PD and 12 with MSA were enrolled in the higher-dose cohorts.

Exidavnemab exhibited a favorable pharmacokinetic profile with a half-life in serum of approximately 32 days. The incidence of anti-drug antibodies was negligible. The ratio between cerebrospinal fluid and serum exposure was 0.4% in both PD and MSA participants, indicating a higher brain exposure than is normally seen with antibody therapies.

The pharmacokinetic profile, in conjunction with exidavnemab's high affinity and selectivity for pathological aggregated forms of alpha-synuclein, support the potential for the doses evaluated in EXIST to attain a sustained target engagement to alpha-synuclein.

No serious adverse events (SAEs) related to treatment were reported and no adverse events related to infusion-site reactions or to allergic reactions associated with administration of the study drug were reported. The most frequently reported adverse events after randomization to exidavnemab, which all were reported twice, were gastroesophageal reflux disease, headache and constipation.

"The interim safety review last year gave us the confidence to progress EXIST into the higher-dose cohorts, and we are very pleased that the completed study now confirms the safety and tolerability of exidavnemab in the studied populations. Particularly encouraging is that no infusion-site-related adverse events or allergic reactions associated with study treatment administration were reported at either of the doses tested," said Gabrielle Åhlberg Hillert, Chief Medical Officer at BioArctic.

"These results provide important support for the continued development of exidavnemab, and we look forward to initiating two Phase 2b studies during the first half of 2027, one in Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI) or mild dementia due to Parkinson's disease or Dementia with Lewy Bodies, and one in Multiple System Atrophy," said Johanna Fälting, Chief R&D Officer at BioArctic.

BioArctic is planning to present more data from the EXIST study at an upcoming scientific conference.

This release discusses investigational uses of an agent in development and is not intended to convey conclusions about efficacy or safety. There is no guarantee that such investigational agents will successfully complete clinical development or gain health authority approval.

The information was released for public disclosure, through the agency of the contact person below, on November 23, 2026, at 08:00 am CET.

For further information, please contact: 
Oskar Bosson, Chief Investor Relations & Communications Officer
E-mail: oskar.bosson@bioarctic.com
Telephone: +46 704 107 180

Jenny Ljunggren, External Communications and Investor Relations Manager
E-mail: jenny.ljunggren@bioarctic.com
Telephone: +46 76 013 86 08

About Exidavnemab

Exidavnemab (BAN0805) is a monoclonal antibody drug candidate that is designed to selectively target and eliminate pathological alpha-synuclein aggregates, while sparing the physiological forms. Aggregates of alpha-synuclein participate in neurodegenerative disorders including Parkinson's disease and Multiple System Atrophy (MSA). The goal is to develop a disease modifying treatment that stops or slows the progression of alpha-synucleinopathies e.g. Parkinson's disease and MSA. Exidavnemab has been granted orphan drug designation (ODD) in the US and a positive opinion regarding orphan medicinal product designation (OD) in the EU for the treatment of Multiple System Atrophy (MSA).

About BioArctic AB

BioArctic AB (publ) is a Swedish research-based biopharma company focusing on innovative treatments that can delay or stop the progression of neurodegenerative diseases. The company invented Leqembi® (lecanemab) – the world's first drug proven to slow the progression of the disease and reduce cognitive impairment in early Alzheimer's disease. Leqembi has been developed together with BioArctic's partner Eisai, who are responsible for regulatory interactions and commercialization globally. In addition to Leqembi, BioArctic has a broad research portfolio with antibodies against Parkinson's disease and ALS as well as additional projects against Alzheimer's disease. Several of the projects utilize the company's proprietary BrainTransporter™ technology, which has the potential to actively transport therapies across the blood-brain barrier to enhance the efficacy of the treatment. BioArctic's B share (BIOA B) is listed on Nasdaq Stockholm Large Cap. For further information, please visit www.bioarctic.com.

data.title: LKAB and Stegra extend collaboration on iron ore pellet supply and testing
data.description:
LKAB and Stegra extend collaboration on iron ore pellet supply and testing

LKAB and Stegra extend collaboration on iron ore pellet supply and testing

PR Newswire

STOCKHOLM, Nov. 23, 2026

STOCKHOLM, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- LKAB and Stegra are taking the next step in their collaboration to establish a future supply of direct reduction (DR) quality iron ore pellets to Stegra's integrated green steel plant in Boden.

Building on the earlier announcement regarding planned test deliveries, LKAB and Stegra have now signed a memorandum of understanding with the aim to advance joint work across commercial, technical and logistics areas. This includes work towards a long-term supply agreement, a structured program for testing LKAB's DR quality pellets, and detailed planning for rail-based deliveries between LKAB's operations and Stegra's plant in Boden.

"Our teams have been working together for some time now and taking further steps in this collaboration makes good business sense for both companies, for the region and, more broadly, for Sweden. With our high-quality iron ore, we want to play a significant part in developing competitive, near-zero emission value chains, both to strengthen our own and Sweden's competitiveness in the global industrial transition, and to seriously reduce carbon emissions in our industry", says Johan Menckel, CEO and President, LKAB.

The technical program will evaluate the physical, chemical and metallurgical performance of the pellets under conditions relevant to Stegra's production process.

"Securing high-quality iron ore feedstock from Sweden is something we set out to do right from the start, so to be able to take further steps and deepen the collaboration with LKAB is something that strengthens the Stegra project even further. Additionally, it also strengthens Sweden's industrial value chain and contributes to a more resilient Europe", says Håkan Buskhe, CEO, Stegra.

The collaboration also covers jointly developing and validating the rail logistics set-up for the potential future supply. The collaboration will cover the full logistics chain, including route and terminal interfaces, loading and unloading arrangements, train and wagon requirements, operational planning and contingency arrangements, with the aim of establishing a reliable and efficient flow of iron ore pellets to Boden.

For more information, contact: Karin Hallstan, Head of Communications, Stegra at press@stegra.com or +46 76 842 81 04

data.title: Monte dei Paschi's Board Sends Mixed Signals Over Intesa's $37 Billion Offer
data.description:
By Michael Hennessey

Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena held back from taking a definitive position on Intesa Sanpaolo's $37 billion takeover offer, ahead of the acceptance period starting later this week.

Monte dei Paschi's board on Saturday gave its official opinion on Intesa's buyout offer and said the proposal is at a fair price.

However, the offer doesn't reflect the value of Monte dei Paschi and its prospects for growth and value creation, the board added.

Each shareholder should assess the transaction independently, the board said as it noted that it wasn't making a recommendation to either accept or reject the offer.

Intesa has offered to buy Monte dei Paschi, which is widely considered to be the world's oldest bank still in operation, for around 33.63 billion euros ($36.89 billion) based on Friday's closing prices. Intesa has a market capitalization of around 102.27 billion euros.

The Monte dei Paschi board said it has taken into account improvements made to Intesa's original offer, but said it still doesn't reflect its growth prospects, particularly after the acquisition of Mediobanca.

The projected synergies from the deal of 2.9 billion euros per year also appear high, Monte dei Paschi said.

Monte dei Paschi had previously been looking to fend off Intesa's offer. However, its plans were upended last month when shareholders overwhelmingly rejected twin bids to buy Banca Generali and Banco BPM, proposed by Chief Executive Officer Luigi Lovaglio in an attempt to thwart the takeover.

Intesa is currently offering 1.25 euros in cash and 1.664 of its shares for each Monte dei Paschi share. The exchange ratio was increased to offset an interim dividend that Intesa plans to pay out.

The acceptance period for Intesa's bid will start on Tuesday and end on Jan. 22, unless it is extended.

data.title: Bitcoin Higher After Weekend Dip Buyers Prevent Further Slide
data.description:
By Joseph Wilkins

Bitcoin recovered some ground on Monday after a bruising weekend that saw the flagship cryptocurrency fall to its lowest level in over two years.

Bitcoin was 1% higher at $61,536, recovering after tumbling as low as $55,691 during Saturday's session. Ether was 0.2% higher at $1,718 after a steep fall to $1,560 over the weekend.

Cryptocurrencies and stocks were pressured last week as the AI trade sold off heavily. Bitcoin's relationship with equities has overtaken gold and the dollar as the strongest macro driver in November, Citi's Alex Saunders said. "Bitcoin's three-month correlation with the S&P 500 has risen above its correlation with gold, which has eased but remains positive, while the relationship with the dollar has become less negative," he wrote.

The issue, Saunders added, is that the selloff in crypto has been far larger than the decline in the S&P 500, meaning higher correlation has not translated into a similar magnitude of price action.

Citi lowered its 12-month bitcoin forecast to $99,532 from $113,000 last week on lower exchange-traded fund demand and a tighter macroeconomic backdrop.

Dip buyers were willing to return to bitcoin when the price fell to near $55,000, said Linh Tran at multiasset broker XS.com. But expectations of interest-rate hikes, a still-strong dollar and continued ETF outflows keep the outlook cautious. Over the next few sessions, Tran said he expects bitcoin to trade around $60,000.

data.title: Stora Enso publishes information brochure on the demerger process and Bergslagets Skogar as a standalone company
data.description:
Stora Enso publishes information brochure on the demerger process and Bergslagets Skogar as a standalone company

Stora Enso publishes information brochure on the demerger process and Bergslagets Skogar as a standalone company

PR Newswire

HELSINKI, Finland, Nov. 23, 2026

STORA ENSO OYJ STOCK EXCHANGE RELEASE 23 November 2026 at 9:00 EET

HELSINKI, Finland, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Stora Enso has published an information brochure providing shareholders with additional information on the demerger process and Bergslagets Skogar as a standalone company.

As announced on 30 October 2026, the Board of Directors of Stora Enso Oyj ("Stora Enso" or the "Company") has approved a demerger plan (the "Demerger Plan") concerning the separation of Stora Enso's Swedish forest assets business through a cross-border partial demerger (the "Demerger"). Under the Demerger Plan, all assets, rights, debts and liabilities relating to, or primarily serving, the Swedish forest assets business would be transferred without a liquidation procedure to Bergslagets Skogar AB ("Bergslagets Skogar"), a Swedish public limited liability company to be incorporated in the Demerger. The Board of Directors of Stora Enso has proposed that the Extraordinary General Meeting, convened for 15 December 2026 (the "EGM") would approve the Demerger Plan and resolve on the Demerger as set out in the Demerger Plan, as well as on the other agenda items set out in the notice convening the EGM.

Stora Enso has today published an information brochure containing additional information for its shareholders on the demerger process and Bergslagets Skogar as a standalone company (the "Information Brochure"). The English-language Information Brochure and its Finnish translation are available on Stora Enso's website at storaenso.com/egm2026.

Overview of Bergslagets Skogar
Bergslagets Skogar would be an independent forest company headquartered in Falun, Sweden, owning and managing approximately 1.22 million hectares of land. Its business would comprise the ownership, management, and development of Stora Enso's forest land in Sweden and related forestry operations, the production of paints and colour pigments, and the management of renewable energy projects. The core commercial activity would be the sale of harvesting rights to industrial customers in the Swedish sawmill and pulp mill industry, complemented by external seedling sales, renewable energy land leases, selected land transactions, and income from land-use rights. Building on its long-term customer arrangements, the business model is designed to preserve long-term forest value while generating recurring cash flows with limited capital expenditure requirements.

Carve-out financial information on Bergslagets Skogar
The Information Brochure includes Bergslagets Skogar's unaudited combined financial statements as at and for the years ended 31 December 2025 and 2024, prepared in accordance with IFRS Accounting Standards as adopted by the EU, and its unaudited condensed combined interim financial information as at and for the nine months ended 30 September 2026, with comparative information for the nine months ended 30 September 2025, prepared in accordance with IAS 34 Interim Financial Reporting. This financial information has not been audited or reviewed by an auditor.

Selected carve-out financial information on Stora Enso
The Information Brochure also includes selected unaudited illustrative financial information for Stora Enso excluding Bergslagets Skogar for the financial year ended 31 December 2025 and the nine months ended 30 September 2026. This information illustrates the hypothetical effects of the Demerger on Stora Enso's consolidated income statements as if the Demerger had occurred on 1 January 2025 (including the September 2025 divestment of approximately 175,000 hectares of Swedish forest land) and 1 January 2026, respectively, and on its consolidated statements of financial position as if the Demerger had occurred on 31 December 2025 and 30 September 2026, respectively.

Completion of the Demerger and first day of trading
The planned date of registration of the completion of the Demerger is 31 March 2027, subject to, among other things, approval by the EGM. Trading in the shares of Bergslagets Skogar on the regulated markets of Nasdaq Stockholm and Nasdaq Helsinki is planned to commence as soon as possible thereafter.

Previous related announcements:

  • 2 November 2026: Notice of the Extraordinary General Meeting of Stora Enso Oyj
  • 30 October 2026: Stora Enso's Board of Directors approves demerger plan to separate Bergslagets Skogar into a new listed company, announcing strategic targets and dividend policy
  • 6 March 2026: Stora Enso presents executive management team for the new forest asset company
  • 8 January 2026: Proposed members to the Board of Directors of the new forest company planned to be separated from Stora Enso

For more information about the demerger, please visit the Demerger info page.


Bergslagets Skogar would be an independent forest company based in the heart of Sweden's forest economy. The company will be focused on creating long-term value from forests for our stakeholders, society and nature. Built on deep expertise based on science and advanced forestry practices, the company will manage its forests as living, evolving systems to support their resilience and productivity over generations. The company will continuously explore new ways for forests to contribute economically, socially and environmentally, from harvest rights and renewable raw materials to recreation, biodiversity and climate benefits, and other ecosystem services. bergslaget.com

Stora Enso is a global leader in renewable materials with a strong focus on packaging. Our purpose is to replace non-renewable materials with renewable solutions. Together with our customers, we design and deliver competitive, high-quality packaging materials and solutions, made from fresh and recycled fibers, accelerating the transition to a circular bioeconomy. Stora Enso has approximately 19,000 employees and our sales in 2025 were EUR 9.3 billion. storaenso.com

data.title: Ant Group’s AI App Afu Open Sources Medical and Health AI Model Family
data.description:
Ant Group’s AI App Afu Open Sources Medical and Health AI Model Family

Ant Group’s AI health app Afu today announced the launch of LingSante, a comprehensive medical and health AI model family, marking a significant step in applying advanced artificial intelligence to healthcare services. Built on the Ant Ling foundational model and applied at scale on the Afu app—which now serves 150 million users and handles nearly 20 million health consultations daily—the new models introduce specialized capabilities ranging from personal health management to complex clinical reasoning.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261122564652/en/

The LingSante family spans a wide spectrum of capabilities, from multimodal understanding and complex medical reasoning to disease risk prediction, safety guardrails, and agentic interaction. At its core are two open-sourced models designed for distinct scenarios:

  • LingSante-3.1-air-VL: A lightweight, native multimodal model tailored for personal users and smaller institutions. It features 124 billion total parameters with 5.5 billion active parameters per token, ensuring efficiency for on-device and localized deployment. The model natively supports text, image, and video inputs, significantly strengthening capabilities in medical image understanding, skin-condition analysis, diet and nutrition assessment, and medical report interpretation.
  • LingSante-3.1-flash: A professional-grade deep-reasoning model aimed at complex clinical tasks. With 560 billion total parameters and approximately 25 billion active parameters per token, it supports a context window of up to 1 million tokens. This model enhances medical knowledge understanding, evidence-based retrieval, and long-horizon workflow execution, making it suitable for complex case analysis and professional medical agent scenarios.

To support a broader range of medical applications, Afu is also introducing specialized models. LingSante-Pulse is a health-prediction model capable of assessing risk for more than 150 conditions by integrating diverse health signals, while LingSante-MedGuard is a safety model designed to identify and mitigate risks related to medical safety, regulatory compliance, and bioethics.

Complementing these is LingSante-Live, a real-time multimodal agent inspired by the traditional Chinese medicine principle of “look, listen, ask, and analyze.” The agent enables an AI video consultation experience and is already integrated into the Afu app. It allows users to initiate video calls, enabling the AI to visually assess symptoms, examine physical conditions, review medications and medical reports, and provide real-time guidance.

As part of its commitment to open source, Afu will open the weights of the model family in phases, starting today with the debut of two core models: LingSante-3.1-air-VL and LingSante-3.1-flash. Interested developers and healthcare researchers can visit Hugging Face to learn more about the models.

  • LingSante-3.1-air-VL: https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/LingSante-3.1-air-VL
  • LingSante-3.1-flash: https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/LingSante-3.1-flash

Beyond the model releases, Ant Group is also advancing industry-wide evaluation standards. Alongside researchers from 29 global institutions, including Stanford University, Harvard University, and Peking Union Medical College, Ant Group launched InclusionMed, an open evaluation and analytics platform dedicated to medical and health AI. In the platform’s inaugural rankings, LingSante-3.1-flash secured the number-one position among all open-source medical and health models, validating its advanced capabilities in real-world clinical tasks.

About Ant Group

Ant Group is a global digital technology provider and the operator of Alipay, a leading internet services platform in China, connecting over one billion users to more than 10,000 types of consumer services from partners. Through innovative products and solutions powered by AI, blockchain and other technologies, Ant Group supports partners across industries to thrive through digital transformation in an ecosystem for inclusive and sustainable development. For more information, visit www.antgroup.com.

data.title: Week Ahead for FX, Bonds: Flash PMI Data to Provide Gauge on Economic Growth
data.description:
By Dow Jones Newswires staff

Below are the most important global events likely to affect FX and bond markets in the week starting Nov. 23.

November's flash purchasing managers' surveys for the U.S., eurozone and U.K. will be among the key events. The surveys are an important measure of economic activity and could signal whether there is scope for the Federal Reserve, European Central Bank and Bank of England to raise interest rates further.

In the U.S, markets will also be closely monitoring Personal Consumption Expenditures price data, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation measure.

In the Asia-Pacific region, South Korea's interest-rate decision will lead the week, with most analysts expecting a quarter-point increase as strong chip exports fuel growth and inflation remains above target. Inflation data from Australia and Tokyo, along with remarks from a Bank of Japan policy board member, could shape expectations for rate increases in both countries.

China will report October industrial profits as investors watch for Beijing's response to tighter U.S. chip export restrictions.

U.S.

U.S. economic activity and inflation will help investors gauge the path of interest rates in a week shortened by a major holiday.

November's flash manufacturing and services PMI numbers are on tap Monday, as well as a speech by New York Federal Reserve President John Williams at the University of Mount Saint Vincent.

September housing indicators are likely to draw attention Tuesday, as elevated mortgage rates weigh on the sector.

The Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index is also scheduled for Tuesday, as consumption continues to be a source of strength for the U.S. economy.

A second estimate of third-quarter gross domestic product growth is due Wednesday. The same day will bring the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, the Personal Consumption Expenditures, as consumer prices keep rising faster than the 2% annual pace targeted by the central bank.

"The main message from the report is likely to be that pressure on goods prices is growing," economists at the Investment Institute by UniCredit said in a note. "Overall, October PCE data are likely to keep the Fed firmly on a hiking trajectory."

Durable goods orders, initial jobless claims and new home sales data are also due Wednesday along with the Summary of Commentary on Current Economic Conditions by Federal Reserve District, known as the Beige Book.

Markets will be closed on Thursday for Thanksgiving Holiday and will close early on Friday.

U.K.

The U.K. will have a relatively light data release calendar. The November flash estimate purchasing managers' index survey on Monday is the main event.

The U.K. composite PMI, a measure of manufacturing and services activity, rose to 52.9 in October, up from 52.0 in September and the highest reading since February.

"For the November report we imagine that the PMIs ticked higher again," Investec economists said in a note.

Activity might have received a boost from the absence of significant tax increases in the U.K. budget in October as some had feared, they said. U.S. President Trump refraining from renewed large-scale attacks on Iran following the midterm elections might have also helped, not least by helping to lower crude prices, they said. Investec forecasts the composite PMI will rise to 53.1 in November.

Elsewhere, the CBI distributive trades survey is due on Wednesday.

The U.K., meanwhile, plans to sell September 2049 index-linked gilt through syndicated sale, subject to demand and market conditions.

Eurozone

German, French and wider eurozone flash purchasing managers' surveys for November are due on Monday. The eurozone composite purchasing managers index, a measure of manufacturing and services activity, fell to a four-month low of 51.7 in October from 53.1 in September but remained above the 50 level that separates an expansion from a contraction.

"We expect to see some mild weakness in the euro-area PMIs, reflecting the challenging environment for energy markets and tighter financial conditions in Europe," RBC Capital Markets strategists said in a note.

On Tuesday, the German ifo business confidence survey for November will be released. That will be followed by the final third-quarter German gross domestic product report on Wednesday and GfK German consumer confidence survey for December on Thursday.

French and Spanish inflation data for November will be published Friday along with November German labor market data and the European Commission's business confidence survey.

Japan

Bank of Japan policy board member Naoki Tamura will meet with local leaders in the Yamanashi prefecture on Thursday. Investors will watch his remarks for clues on when the central bank might raise rates again.

Tokyo's November consumer-price data are due Friday. The figures are an early indicator of nationwide inflation, and a pickup could strengthen expectations for a rate increase.

BOJ Gov. Kazuo Ueda recently stressed the importance of keeping underlying inflation around the central bank's 2% target. He said inflation excluding fresh food is likely to rise well above 2% as companies pass on higher labor costs, oil prices remain high and the yen stays weak.

The Ministry of Finance will auction about 300 billion yen of 40-year government bonds on Wednesday, reopening an issue first sold in May. The sale could draw demand from insurers and pension funds seeking long-dated debt.

The BOJ is scheduled to buy government bonds in three maturity ranges on Thursday, including those with more than three and up to five years remaining and those with more than 10 and up to 25 years remaining.

Japanese markets will be closed Monday for a national holiday.

China

A thin data slate awaits in China. The sole release of note drops Friday, which will show how China's industrial firms fared in October.

Economists will look at the figures to see if industrial profit growth held up last month after surging in September. Spending tied to artificial intelligence and digital infrastructure has been a key driver of profits over the year, though that hasn't benefited all sectors evenly.

Focus will also be on any potential announcements from Beijing after Xi Jinping's meetings with Trump didn't yield much in the way of progress on key trade and geopolitical issues. Markets will be watching ministry statements closely after Chinese officials warned of potential countermeasures to U.S. moves to tighten chip-export restrictions.

Australia / New Zealand

Australia's October inflation report on Wednesday will help shape expectations for the Reserve Bank of Australia's December rate decision. In September, annual headline inflation rose to 4.3% and trimmed-mean inflation climbed to 3.6%.

Third-quarter capital spending data due Thursday will show how much businesses invested and whether they revised their spending plans. The RBA will publish its bulletin the same day.

In New Zealand, third-quarter retail sales data due Monday will show how household spending is holding up ahead of the central bank's Dec. 9 rate decision.

South Korea

Bank of Korea is expected to raise its benchmark rate by a quarter-percentage-point to 3.25% on Thursday after leaving it unchanged in October.

Some analysts also expect the bank to raise its growth and inflation forecasts for 2026 and 2027 as demand for chips used in artificial intelligence boosts exports and price pressures persist.

The central bank signaled it would raise its growth forecasts after third-quarter gross domestic product grew faster than expected. It expects inflation to stay above its 2% target through 2027.

The International Monetary Fund, the Korea Development Institute and Citi Research raised their growth forecasts for South Korea earlier this month, citing strength in the semiconductor industry.

Singapore

Singapore's consumer-price index likely rose 1.9% in October from a year earlier, down from 2.2% in September, according to the median estimate of six economists polled by The Wall Street Journal. Core inflation, which excludes private road transport and accommodation costs, likely slowed to 1.6% from 2.0%, the poll showed. The data are due Monday.

Lower fourth-quarter electricity tariffs and a high year-earlier comparison likely helped ease inflation, said UOB economist Jester Koh.

Final third-quarter gross domestic product figures are due Tuesday. An advance estimate showed the economy grew 5.4% from a year earlier. DBS economists expect that figure to be revised up to 5.6%, mainly because manufacturing grew faster than initially reported.

DBS expects the government to forecast growth of 2.5% to 4.5% for 2027.

Any references to days are in local times.

data.title: Battalion Advanced Technology Ltd: Battalion commits up to £3 million to UK hypersonic materials programme with Oxford Sigma
data.description:
Battalion Advanced Technology Ltd: Battalion commits up to £3 million to UK hypersonic materials programme with Oxford Sigma

Battalion Advanced Technology Ltd: Battalion commits up to £3 million to UK hypersonic materials programme with Oxford Sigma

PR Newswire

LONDON, Nov. 23, 2026

Programme SPEAR addresses three engineering problems that limit hypersonic flight. The intellectual property it creates will be owned by Battalion, a UK company.

LONDON, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Battalion Advanced Technology Ltd ("Battalion") has signed a research agreement with Oxford Sigma Limited ("Oxford Sigma") to develop materials and component technologies for hypersonic applications. Programme SPEAR has up to £3 million committed over three years and will be carried out in the UK.

Materials performance is a critical challenge in hypersonic flight to enable better performance and capability. Heat, pressure and oxidation place demanding requirements on joints, seals and apertures. SPEAR focuses on three related engineering challenges: joining dissimilar materials, developing adaptive seals and creating windows that maintain their performance in extreme environments.

Oxford Sigma will carry out the research under Principal Investigator Dr Thomas P. Davis, drawing on its existing materials expertise and know-how. Battalion will own the intellectual property created through SPEAR and lead its commercialisation, with Oxford Sigma entitled to 1.5% royalties on qualifying future product sales and licensing income under the agreement.

Alongside new intellectual property, the programme aims to produce prototype hardware, supporting test evidence and manufacturing know-how, establishing a foundation for subsequent qualification and commercial development. Technologies will be assessed progressively, with investment focused on those offering the strongest technical and commercial potential.

Oxford Sigma brings together materials development, computational modelling, prototype manufacture and experimental testing within a single British-owned UK organisation. Its experience across fusion, nuclear and defence engineering enables the programme to consider manufacturing, verification and future qualification requirements from the outset, alongside materials performance.

The programme is designed to take technologies from early-stage research (Technology Readiness Level 2-3) to TRL 4-5, including the testing of prototypes and potential products under Battalion's direction. SPEAR will be coordinated with the hypersonic materials programme Battalion directs and funds at The Pennsylvania State University in the United States, and is aligned with AUKUS Pillar II, under which the UK, US, and Australia cooperate on advanced capabilities including hypersonics.

R. Michael Jones, Co-founder and Director of Battalion, commented:

"National security problems do not stop at borders, and the work on them should not either. SPEAR puts a British team on three of the hardest problems in hypersonic flight, alongside the programme we direct at Penn State. Allies attacking the same problem from different angles is how this moves quickly."

Dr Thomas P. Davis, Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer of Oxford Sigma, commented:

"Hypersonic flight and fusion energy share an opportunity: materials operating beyond the limits of conventional engineering. Our team has spent years developing materials and components for those conditions. SPEAR focuses that expertise on three defined materials themes, with a partner committed to taking the results towards practical applications."

About Programme SPEAR

Programme SPEAR is a research programme funded and directed by Battalion and carried out by Oxford Sigma over up to three years. It is staged, from research to prototypes and demonstrators, with progress reviews directing investment to the strongest technologies.

About Oxford Sigma

Oxford Sigma is a British-owned, internationally recognised advanced materials company based in Oxford, UK, focused on fusion, nuclear and defence systems. It is a supplier under the UK Ministry of Defence's Hypersonic Technologies & Capability Development Framework (HTCDF), with wider experience across UK defence research and weapons engineering programmes. Dr Thomas P. Davis, Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer, is Principal Investigator for Programme SPEAR. His background spans materials science, fusion engineering, defence materials, and materials standardisation. He holds a PhD (DPhil) in Materials Science from the University of Oxford.

About Battalion

Battalion Advanced Technology Ltd is a London-based company that develops hypersonic materials and wide-bandgap semiconductor devices for national security and dual-use applications. It directs and funds the underlying research at The Pennsylvania State University, ranked first in the United States for materials science research expenditures (NSF, FY 2024), and at Oxford Sigma in the UK through Programme SPEAR.

data.title: Q3 2026 Earnings Release: Cadeler Delivers Robust Revenue Growth Alongside Continued Strong Execution and Investments in Its Full-Scope Foundation Installation Capabilities
data.description:
Q3 2026 Earnings Release: Cadeler Delivers Robust Revenue Growth Alongside Continued Strong Execution and Investments in Its Full-Scope Foundation Installation Capabilities

Cadeler has published its Q3 2026 Earnings Release, reflecting continued strong performance, with revenue for the third quarter up by 65% compared to the same period in 2025. The quarter saw further expansion of the fleet and of the company’s capabilities: In July, Cadeler took delivery of its second A-class vessel, Wind Ace, and in August it acquired Menck, strengthening its full-scope foundation installation offering.

Revenue for the first nine months of 2026 reached EUR 663 million, up 94% from EUR 342 million for the same period last year, while EBITDA was EUR 321 million, up 52% from EBITDA of EUR 211 million in 2025 (in each case, when adjusting for one-off termination fees of EUR 111 million in the comparative period).

Profit for the first nine months of 2026 was EUR 143 million, up 18% from EUR 121 million in the comparative period, when adjusting for the termination fees identified above.

Utilisation of Cadeler’s 11 vessels was 69.8%, compared with 75.8% across eight operating vessels over the same period last year, while contracted days increased by 44%, reflecting increased activity across the enlarged fleet.

Cadeler maintains its full-year 2026 guidance, with full-year revenue expected to be within the range of EUR 910 million to 1,000 million, which includes an anticipated hammer sale scheduled to complete in December 2026. Full-year EBITDA is expected to be within the range of EUR 435 million to 525 million, when excluding costs related to the acquisition and integration of Menck.

Mikkel Gleerup, CEO of Cadeler, comments:

“These results demonstrate that our strategy is translating into strong execution and continued growth. During the period, we have delivered solid operational and financial performance, welcomed Wind Ace to our fleet and, through the acquisition of Menck, significantly strengthened the capabilities we can offer within full-scope foundation transport and installation. Together, these developments give us greater flexibility to respond to changing project requirements and support our customers with the reliability, resilience and certainty of delivery they increasingly require. With a strong backlog and continued demand for our vessels and services, we remain focused on disciplined execution across our projects while building the capabilities required for the next phase of offshore wind development.”

Acquisition of Menck

Cadeler completed the acquisition of Menck in August 2026 for an enterprise value of EUR 501 million. The acquisition combines Menck’s specialist equipment and engineering expertise with Cadeler’s installation fleet and experience, enabling a more integrated foundation installation offering for the group’s customers. Menck continues to operate as a standalone business, preserving its independent market position. The transaction was financed through available liquidity and a EUR 380 million acquisition facility. Menck contributed approximately EUR 24.1 million of revenue and EUR 1.1 million of net profit from 11 August to 30 September 2026.

Backlog and commercial momentum

As of 23 November 2026, Cadeler’s contract backlog, including options, stands at EUR 2.4 billion.

The backlog includes a firm contract, signed after the reporting period, to support the transportation and installation of wind turbines at Dogger Bank C in the UK, the third 1.2GW phase of the world’s largest offshore wind farm under construction and the operational debut for Wind Apex.

Cadeler also announced the signing of a significant exclusivity agreement (not included in the group’s contract backlog) with an undisclosed client for wind turbine and foundation installation at a large-scale offshore wind farm in the UK. That installation campaign is expected to commence in 2030, with the foundations campaign to be executed using an A-class vessel and an O-class vessel, and the wind turbines to be installed by a P-class vessel.

Fleet expansion and newbuild programme

By mid-2027, Cadeler expects to operate a 12-vessel fleet, the largest and most versatile in the offshore wind industry.

Wind Ace joined the fleet in July 2026 on schedule and within budget. Designed for both foundation and turbine installation, its first project will be ScottishPower Renewables’ East Anglia TWO, where offshore installation is planned to begin in 2027. The construction of Cadeler’s third A-class vessel, Wind Apex, is similarly progressing on schedule.

In August, Cadeler signed firm contracts with COSCO Shipping Offshore for two T-class vessels, due for delivery in 2030 and 2031. Incorporating breakthrough technologies, the T-class vessels will be the largest and most capable vessels in the offshore installation and foundation market.

Redomiciliation to the United Kingdom

Cadeler successfully completed its redomiciliation to the United Kingdom on 4 November 2026, following acceptance of the voluntary share exchange offer by holders representing 92.06% of Cadeler A/S shares. Cadeler plc’s shares began trading on the Oslo and New York stock exchanges on 5 November 2026. Cadeler plc intends to acquire the remaining 7.94% of Cadeler A/S shares for approximately EUR 173 million. The establishment of a UK-incorporated parent company positions the Group to attract a broader and more diverse international investor base, while creating a corporate structure that better reflects the scale and global reach of Cadeler’s activities. The redomiciliation will have no impact on Cadeler’s personnel, geographic footprint or project operations.

Strong balance sheet and strategic financing initiatives

As of 30 September 2026, Cadeler’s total assets stood at EUR 4.5 billion, up 31+% year-to-date. This includes a EUR 484 million increase in property, plant and equipment, primarily attributable to newbuilds and various vessel upgrades, as well as the acquisition of Menck. Total equity increased to EUR 1.9 billion as of 30 September 2026, reflecting an increase of EUR 347 million from the balance at year end 2025 of EUR 1.5 billion.

In July 2026, Cadeler announced the signing of an EIFO-backed green term loan facility of EUR 247 million to fund the delivery of Wind Apex, expected in Q2 2027.

Earnings Call

In connection with the publication of its Q3 2026 Earnings Release, Cadeler will host a live video webcast presentation for the investment community. Mikkel Gleerup, Chief Executive Officer, and Peter Brogaard Hansen, Chief Financial Officer, will present live from London.

Date: 23 November 2026
Time: 08:00 EST / 13:00 UK / 14:00 CET

The earnings presentation is open to all interested parties and may include forward-looking information. Please register in advance at this link https://cadeler-q3-2026-earnings-presentation.open-exchange.net/registration.

A replay of the webcast and the presentation slides will be made available on Cadeler’s Investor Relations website following the presentation, available here: http://www.cadeler.com/investor.

About Cadeler:

Cadeler plc (Cadeler) is a global leader in offshore wind turbine transport and installation. The company owns and operates the industry’s largest fleet of jack-up offshore wind installation vessels and is expanding its capabilities into full-scope foundation transport and installation, as well as operations & maintenance. With its modern fleet and depth of expertise across onshore and offshore operations, Cadeler supports the safe, efficient and reliable delivery of offshore wind projects worldwide. Cadeler is listed on both the New York Stock Exchange and the Oslo Stock Exchange, under the ticker “CDLR”. For more information, please visit www.cadeler.com.

AADX Investors Have Opportunity to Join Applied Aerospace & Defense, Inc. Fraud Investigation with SBS Law

PR Newswire

LOS ANGELES, Nov. 23, 2026

LOS ANGELES, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Schall, Brown & Schwartz LLP ("SBS"), a national shareholder rights litigation firm, announces that it is investigating claims on behalf of investors of Applied Aerospace & Defense, Inc. ("Applied Aerospace" or "the Company") (NYSE: AADX) for violations of the securities laws.

INVESTIGATION DETAILS: The investigation focuses on whether the Company issued false and/or misleading statements and/or failed to disclose information pertinent to investors. Applied Aerospace failed to inform investors of constraints on supply for specialized components. The Company misled shareholders about delays in approval for the overhaul program for Apache helicopter rotor heads, which led to delays in revenue recognition. The Company suffered harsh ramp costs that impacted its gross profit margin. Based on these facts, shares of Applied Aerospace fell sharply.
